searches.reason: Develop paired intervention probes that test whether recommendations depend on recent, repeated interests or stale associations. Compare original histories with recent-item masking, older-history masking, order shuffling, and matched-user history swaps. Measure rank changes and top-10 overlap, using length-matched controls and bootstrap uncertainty. These probes could identify whether sequence encoding, positional information, or personalization needs improvement without treating sensitivity alone as evidence of quality.
searches.query: sequential recommendation counterfactual diagnostic probes recent intent history truncation order permutation user history swaps temporal sensitivity controlled interventions 2024 2025 2026

searches.reason: Replace training-margin diagnostics with scale-independent ranking stress tests using training-only held-out prefixes, unseen full-catalog candidates, and hard negatives matched by interaction popularity or title/description similarity. Investigate how reliably these probes predict the fixed validation HR@10 across all four datasets, keeping the host evaluator unchanged. This should reveal failures hidden by easy sampled negatives and distinguish item-scoring problems from candidate-sampling artifacts.
searches.query: recommender evaluation sampled negatives full catalog ranking bias hard negative diagnostic stress tests popularity matched semantic negatives sequential recommendation 2024 2025 2026

searches.reason: Build an evidence-grounded feedback taxonomy for the twenty training users: immediate relevance, broad association, possible redundancy, explicit specification conflict, and insufficient evidence. Use only histories, timestamps, titles, descriptions, and supplied qualitative feedback; leave compatibility, ownership satisfaction, and preference rejection uncertain unless supported. Research agreement, abstention, and uncertainty estimation so these judgments can guide model changes without inventing unavailable attributes or conflating relatedness with usefulness.
